headline: High-risk filesystem and network-enabled OpenHands paired with local-only Taipy creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write mounted files and use MCP, so taipy outputs placed in a shared workspace could be treated as instructions. Taipy has no documented input hardening or isolation, so the pairwise bridge is plausible even though direct ingestion is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF taipy output is copied into a mounted file or MCP-fed prompt that OpenHands reads
IF both agents share the same writable volume without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Disable MCP for the OpenHands runtime
Add a manual review step before OpenHands consumes taipy output
Prefix taipy artifacts with non-executable markers
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches mounted files and has broad network egress, while taipy is documented as local-only network-wise. If sensitive files are mounted into OpenHands, its outputs or context can leave the workspace via configured model providers or MCP. Taipy itself does not show a leak path, so the main risk is OpenHands-mediated exposure.
conditions: IF sensitive files are mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands is configured with an external model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the mounted workspace
Use a local model provider for OpenHands
Disable MCP servers unless needed
Mount read-only inputs only
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive data into a separate runtime

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can write the filesystem and modify git state inside its Docker runtime; the profile says shared state with other instances is via mounted volume only. Taipy has no write capability documented, but if both are pointed at the same mounted workspace, OpenHands can overwrite artifacts Taipy reads or produces. The conflict is plausible but not proven high because Taipy write surfaces are absent.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory
IF taipy reads or serves files that OpenHands can rewrite
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Make the shared mount read-only for one agent
Avoid concurrent git operations
Add a lock file around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: introduce orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code or file edits that taipy may consume as pipeline inputs, but taipy has no documented verification gate or critical-evaluation behavior. If taipy treats OpenHands output as authoritative, a bad edit can cascade into downstream automation or data workflows. The interaction is inferred from OpenHands' agent loop and taipy's automation role, so uncertainty remains.
conditions: IF taipy ingests OpenHands-produced files or parameters without validation
IF OpenHands is allowed to write artifacts that taipy later executes or schedules
mitigations: Require schema validation on taipy inputs
Add a human approval step before execution
Compare OpenHands outputs against a known-good baseline
Log and diff generated artifacts before use
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not document conflicting residency, retention, or certification constraints. OpenHands handles model-provider API keys and mounted files, while taipy lists no sensitive data classes or compliance restrictions. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is limited to configuration gaps rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is mounted into OpenHands without a matching policy for the configured model provider
IF taipy is later configured to process regulated data under stricter residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review provider terms for OpenHands
Document retention settings for both tools
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency
